name: Webdispečink Fleet
description: Reads vehicles, drivers, positions and the log book from the Webdispečink SOAP API 2.0 and WRITES them onto the raw signal lane via wd_upsert_*_audited. Kept alongside the Eurowag plugin rather than replaced by it: measured against the same tenant, this endpoint returns every vehicle (14 vs 6) and the driver identity the successor omits — Dallas chip, personnel number, division, assigned plate. Optional by construction: a deployment that never touches Webdispečink simply does not install it.
author: Evymo

url.description: SOAP 2.0 endpoint (rpc/literal). There is no REST surface; every operation is a POST here.

kodf.description: Customer code. Sent on EVERY call together with username and pass — the API keeps no session, so there is nothing to log in to once.

password.description: Password OR a user token — the vendor accepts a token in place of the password, in the same field (not as a bearer header).

positionPollSeconds.description: How often to read all vehicle positions. Positions change continuously; the log book does not, and is pulled on demand.

fleetSyncCron.description: Vehicles and drivers are a codebook, not a stream: daily is enough.

geocodePositions.description: Ask the vendor to resolve each position to an address. Billed per lookup on their side, so off unless someone asks for it.

includeDisabledDrivers.description: Keep drivers the vendor flagged disabled. A past trip still belongs to whoever drove it, so dropping them would orphan history.

rideSyncCron.description: When to pull the log book. Deliberately AFTER fleetSyncCron: the work list for rides is the vehicle registry, so a ride sync over an empty registry would have nothing to read.

rideBackfillDays.description: How far back the FIRST run reaches when no cursor exists yet. Later runs read from the stored cursor, so history is not re-fetched every night.

ridePauseMs.description: Pause between per-vehicle log book calls. The log book is per vehicle, so the fleet size IS the request count — this is courtesy toward someone else's production system, not our own throttling.

rideCallBudget.description: Hard ceiling on log book calls per tick, 0 = none. A grown fleet or a misread cursor must not turn one tick into hundreds of vendor requests. When the budget stops a run, the cursor is held back so the window is retried rather than skipped.

worktimeSyncCron.description: When to pull driver tachograph worktime (_getDriverWorkTacho). After the ride sync — worktime is per driver, keyed on the driver codebook. Reuses ridePauseMs / rideCallBudget for the per-driver call discipline.

worktimeBackfillDays.description: How far back the FIRST worktime run reaches when no cursor exists yet. Later runs read from the stored cursor.

overspeedSyncCron.description: When to pull overspeed segments (_getCarOverSpeed). Per vehicle, reuses ride cursor/pause/budget discipline.

driverStatsSyncCron.description: When to pull driver statistics (_getStaDrivers) — fleet-wide, one call. Stores one snapshot per driver.

driverStatsWindowDays.description: Rolling window (days) the driver-stats snapshot aggregates over — align with the surface's worktime window so the two match.

rideOverlapHours.description: Each daily ride sync re-reads this many hours before the stored cursor, so rides the vendor edited after the fact (private/business, corrected distance) are picked up. Costs rows, not calls (one call per vehicle either way).

worktimeOverlapHours.description: Same overlap for daily tachograph work summaries: the current day is still growing and verified days arrive later.

projectionWindowMin.description: Rides and work days touched by sync within this many minutes are re-offered to the twin projection, which writes only what actually changed.
